questions.text: How many classes of food are there in total?
questions.explanation: There are 6 classes of food: carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, and water.

questions.text: Which class of food is the body's main source of energy?
questions.explanation: Carbohydrates are the body's main source of energy.

questions.text: Protein is mainly needed in the body for
questions.explanation: Proteins are essential for body building and tissue repair.

questions.text: Which vitamin deficiency causes scurvy?
questions.explanation: Scurvy is caused by a deficiency of vitamin C.

questions.text: Night blindness is caused by the deficiency of
questions.explanation: Night blindness is caused by a deficiency of vitamin A.

questions.text: Which of these is a source of roughage?
questions.explanation: Vegetables are a good source of roughage (dietary fibre).

questions.text: Water is classified as a nutrient because it
questions.explanation: Water is essential for various body functions even though it provides no energy.

questions.text: Fats and oils belong to the class of food known as
questions.explanation: Fats and oils belong to the lipids class of food.

questions.text: Which of these is a simple carbohydrate?
questions.explanation: Glucose is a simple sugar (monosaccharide), a simple carbohydrate.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "Starch is an example of" by choosing the correct option.
questions.explanation: Starch is a polysaccharide, which is a complex carbohydrate.

questions.text: Which mineral is essential for strong bones and teeth?
questions.explanation: Calcium is essential for building and maintaining strong bones and teeth.

questions.text: Iron deficiency in the body leads to
questions.explanation: Iron deficiency leads to anaemia, a condition of low haemoglobin.

questions.text: Which of these is a function of fat in the body?
questions.explanation: Fats serve as a concentrated source of energy and provide body insulation.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "A balanced diet contains" by choosing the correct option.
options: All classes of food in correct proportions
questions.explanation: A balanced diet provides all classes of food in the right proportions.

questions.text: Goitre is caused by the deficiency of
questions.explanation: Goitre is caused by iodine deficiency, leading to enlargement of the thyroid gland.

questions.text: Which of these is NOT a method of food preservation?
questions.explanation: Boiling is a cooking method, not a preservation method.

questions.text: Rickets is caused by the deficiency of
questions.explanation: Rickets is caused by a deficiency of vitamin D, leading to weak bones in children.

questions.text: Which food group does beans belong to?
questions.explanation: Beans belong to the protein food group as they are rich in plant protein.

questions.text: Vitamins are needed in the body mainly for
questions.explanation: Vitamins mainly regulate body processes and protect against diseases.

questions.text: Which of these is a source of vitamin C?
questions.explanation: Oranges are a rich source of vitamin C.

questions.text: The unit of measuring energy in food is
questions.explanation: Calorie (or kilocalorie) is the unit used to measure energy in food.

questions.text: Which of these is a Nigerian staple food?
questions.explanation: Yam is a major staple food in Nigeria.

questions.text: Boiling uses which medium to cook food?
questions.explanation: Boiling uses hot water as the cooking medium.

questions.text: Which of these kitchen utensils is used for mixing ingredients?
questions.explanation: A whisk is used for mixing, beating, and whipping ingredients.

questions.text: The food safety regulatory agency in Nigeria is
questions.explanation: NAFDAC (National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control) regulates food safety in Nigeria.

questions.text: Roughage in food is important because it
questions.explanation: Roughage (dietary fibre) aids digestion and helps prevent constipation.

questions.text: Which of these is a source of protein?
questions.explanation: Fish is an excellent source of animal protein.

questions.text: Vitamin A is important for the maintenance of
questions.explanation: Vitamin A is essential for good vision and healthy eyes.

questions.text: Which of these is a function of water in the body?
questions.explanation: Water helps regulate body temperature through sweating and evaporation.

questions.text: Which cooking method uses hot oil to cook food?
questions.explanation: Frying uses hot oil as the cooking medium.

questions.text: Carbohydrates are broken down in the body to form
questions.explanation: Carbohydrates are broken down into glucose, which provides energy.

questions.text: Which of the following is a complete protein source?
questions.explanation: Eggs contain all essential amino acids, making them a complete protein source.

questions.text: Beriberi is caused by the deficiency of
questions.explanation: Beriberi is caused by a deficiency of thiamine (vitamin B1).

questions.text: Which of these foods is rich in vitamin D?
questions.explanation: Milk and cod liver oil are rich sources of vitamin D.

questions.text: The process of cooking food in steam from boiling water is called
questions.explanation: Steaming involves cooking food using steam from boiling water.

questions.text: Pellagra is caused by the deficiency of
questions.explanation: Pellagra is caused by a deficiency of niacin (vitamin B3).

questions.text: Which of these is a function of calcium in the body?
questions.explanation: Calcium is needed for building and maintaining strong bones and teeth.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "Food preservation aims to" by choosing the correct option.
options: Prevent food spoilage and extend shelf life
questions.explanation: Food preservation prevents spoilage and extends the shelf life of food.

questions.text: Which of these is a method of dry heat cooking?
questions.explanation: Roasting is a dry heat cooking method that uses hot air in an oven.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "Kwashiorkor is a disease caused by" by choosing the correct option.
questions.explanation: Kwashiorkor is caused by severe protein deficiency, common in children.

questions.text: Which of these is NOT a Nigerian staple?
questions.explanation: Couscous is a West African North African dish, not a Nigerian staple.

questions.text: The recommended number of meals per day for a healthy adult is
questions.explanation: A healthy adult should eat 3 main meals and healthy snacks in between.

questions.text: Which of these minerals helps in blood clotting?
questions.explanation: Calcium plays an important role in blood clotting.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "Marasmus is caused by" by choosing the correct option.
questions.explanation: Marasmus results from a general deficiency of calories and nutrients.

questions.text: Which food group does palm oil belong to?
questions.explanation: Palm oil belongs to the fats and oils food group.

questions.text: Which of these is an advantage of steaming over boiling?
questions.explanation: Steaming retains more nutrients than boiling since food is not submerged in water.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "A menu is defined as" by choosing the correct option.
options: A list of food items available for a meal
questions.explanation: A menu is a list of food items available for selection in a meal.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "Sodium is mainly obtained from" by choosing the correct option.
questions.explanation: Sodium is mainly obtained from table salt (sodium chloride).

questions.text: Which of these is a source of omega-3 fatty acids?
questions.explanation: Oily fish such as salmon and sardines are rich sources of omega-3 fatty acids.

questions.text: What does the abbreviation The BMR stand for in full?
questions.explanation: BMR stands for Basal Metabolic Rate, the minimum energy needed at rest.

questions.text: Which of these is a role of zinc in the body?
questions.explanation: Zinc plays a role in wound healing, growth, and immune function.

questions.text: Smoking is a food preservation method that works by
options: Exposing food to smoke which has antibacterial properties
questions.explanation: Smoking preserves food by exposing it to wood smoke, which has antimicrobial compounds.

questions.text: Which of these is a function of dietary fibre?
options: Prevents constipation and promotes gut health
questions.explanation: Dietary fibre prevents constipation and promotes healthy digestion.

questions.text: What does Pasteurization of milk involve in the context of fishing?
options: Freezing milk at very low temperatures
Heating milk to kill harmful bacteria
questions.explanation: Pasteurization involves heating milk to a specific temperature to kill harmful bacteria.

questions.text: Which kitchen safety rule involves handling sharp objects?
options: Cut away from the body and keep knives sharp
Leave the gas on after cooking
Use wet hands near electrical appliances
questions.explanation: When using sharp objects, always cut away from the body and keep knives sharp to prevent slipping.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "A recipe is best described as" by choosing the correct option.
options: A set of instructions for preparing a dish
questions.explanation: A recipe is a set of step-by-step instructions for preparing a specific dish.

questions.text: Which of these foods is the richest source of vitamin C?
questions.explanation: Guava is one of the richest sources of vitamin C among common fruits.

questions.text: Which of these is a consequence of excessive salt intake?
questions.explanation: Excessive salt intake can lead to high blood pressure (hypertension).

questions.text: The process of preserving food by removing moisture is known as
questions.explanation: Dehydration preserves food by removing most of its moisture content.

questions.text: Carbohydrate foods are classified into simple and
questions.explanation: Carbohydrates are classified into simple (sugars) and complex (starches).

questions.text: Which of these is NOT a function of fat in the body?
questions.explanation: Transporting oxygen is the function of haemoglobin in red blood cells, not fat.

questions.text: Osteoporosis in adults is associated with the deficiency of
questions.explanation: Osteoporosis (brittle bones) is associated with calcium deficiency, especially in older adults.

questions.text: Which of these is a principle of food hygiene?
options: Wash hands before and after handling food
Store raw and cooked food together
questions.explanation: Washing hands before and after handling food is a key principle of food hygiene.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "Sprouting of grains increases their" by choosing the correct option.
questions.explanation: Sprouting grains increases their vitamin content, particularly B vitamins.

questions.text: Which of these is a function of iodine in the body?
options: Prevents goitre by supporting thyroid function
questions.explanation: Iodine is essential for thyroid gland function and prevents goitre.

questions.text: Which kitchen equipment is used for deep frying?
questions.explanation: A deep fryer or deep pot is used for deep frying food in hot oil.

questions.text: The temperature danger zone for food is between
questions.explanation: The temperature danger zone is between 5C and 63C where bacteria multiply rapidly.

questions.text: An immune-boosting nutrient found abundantly in citrus fruits is
questions.explanation: Vitamin C, found abundantly in citrus fruits, boosts the immune system.

questions.text: Which of these is a factor affecting food choices?
questions.explanation: Culture, religion, economics, and personal preferences are key factors affecting food choices.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "A table napkin is placed" by choosing the correct option.
options: On the lap of the diner
In the centre of the table only
questions.explanation: A table napkin is placed on the lap of the diner during a meal.

questions.text: Which of the following correctly describes an amino acid?
questions.explanation: Amino acids are the building blocks of proteins.

questions.text: Essential amino acids are called so because
options: They are found only in eggs
The body cannot make them and must get them from food
They are the most important nutrients
questions.explanation: Essential amino acids cannot be synthesised by the body and must come from the diet.

questions.text: Which of these is a water-soluble vitamin?
questions.explanation: Vitamin C is a water-soluble vitamin, unlike vitamins A, D, and K which are fat-soluble.

questions.text: Fat-soluble vitamins are stored mainly in the
questions.explanation: Fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K) are stored mainly in the liver.

questions.text: Which process converts starch into sugar during bread making?
questions.explanation: Fermentation by yeast converts starch and sugar into alcohol and carbon dioxide.

questions.text: The Maillard reaction in cooking is responsible for
options: Browning and flavour development on cooked surfaces
questions.explanation: The Maillard reaction causes browning and complex flavour development when proteins and sugars react under heat.

questions.text: Which of these foods has the highest protein content per 100g?
questions.explanation: Lean beef contains approximately 26g of protein per 100g, which is very high.

questions.text: A foodborne illness caused by Salmonella is most commonly associated with
questions.explanation: Salmonella infection is commonly associated with undercooked eggs and poultry products.

questions.text: The process by which the body uses nutrients for growth and maintenance is called
questions.explanation: Metabolism is the sum of all chemical processes by which the body uses nutrients.

questions.text: Which of the following is a disadvantage of canning as a preservation method?
options: It is too expensive for all foods
It may alter the texture and nutrient content of food
questions.explanation: Canning can alter food texture and reduce heat-sensitive nutrient content.

questions.text: Which of these is a characteristic of a well-planned menu?
options: It has variety and nutritional balance
It repeats the same dish daily
questions.explanation: A well-planned menu offers variety and ensures nutritional balance.

questions.text: Fermentation in food production is carried out by
options: Beneficial microorganisms such as yeast and bacteria
questions.explanation: Fermentation is carried out by beneficial microorganisms like yeast and bacteria.

questions.text: Iodized salt was introduced primarily to prevent
questions.explanation: Iodized salt was introduced to prevent goitre and other iodine deficiency disorders.

questions.text: Which of these best describes bioavailability of a nutrient?
options: The amount of nutrient in the food
The proportion of nutrient absorbed and used by the body
The cooking time of the food
questions.explanation: Bioavailability refers to the proportion of a nutrient that is absorbed and utilised by the body.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "Rancidity of fats occurs when" by choosing the correct option.
options: Fats are heated to boiling point
Fats react with oxygen and undergo oxidation
questions.explanation: Rancidity occurs when fats and oils undergo oxidation, producing unpleasant odours and flavours.

questions.text: Which of these is a role of phosphorus in the body?
options: Works with calcium for bone formation
questions.explanation: Phosphorus works alongside calcium in bone and teeth formation.

questions.text: A child who is both malnourished and has oedema most likely suffers from
questions.explanation: Kwashiorkor is characterised by protein deficiency and often presents with oedema (swelling).

questions.text: Which of these is a food additive used as a preservative?
questions.explanation: Sodium benzoate is a common food preservative used to prevent microbial growth.

questions.text: The process of blanching vegetables involves
options: Briefly boiling then plunging into cold water
questions.explanation: Blanching involves briefly boiling vegetables and then plunging them into ice water to stop cooking.

questions.text: Which of these is an advantage of food irradiation?
options: It kills harmful bacteria and extends shelf life
It changes the food's taste completely
questions.explanation: Food irradiation kills harmful microorganisms and extends shelf life without making food radioactive.

questions.text: Which vitamin is synthesised in the skin upon exposure to sunlight?
questions.explanation: Vitamin D is synthesised in the skin when exposed to ultraviolet rays from sunlight.

questions.text: The recommended daily allowance (RDA) of protein for a healthy adult is approximately
questions.explanation: The RDA for protein for healthy adults is about 0.8 to 1g per kilogram of body weight.

questions.text: Which of these is a symptom of vitamin A deficiency other than night blindness?
questions.explanation: Vitamin A deficiency causes dry, rough skin known as follicular hyperkeratosis.

questions.text: Cross-contamination in the kitchen occurs when
options: Food is cooked at the right temperature
Pathogens transfer from raw food to cooked food
Food is stored in clean containers
questions.explanation: Cross-contamination happens when harmful organisms transfer from raw to ready-to-eat foods.

questions.text: Which of these is a source of preformed vitamin A (retinol)?
questions.explanation: Liver is a rich source of preformed vitamin A (retinol), while plants provide beta-carotene.

questions.text: Gelatinisation of starch occurs when
options: Starch is mixed with cold water
Starch granules swell and burst in hot water, thickening the mixture
questions.explanation: Gelatinisation occurs when starch granules absorb hot water, swell, and thicken the mixture.

questions.text: Which of these is a characteristic of a good dietary plan for a pregnant woman?
options: Increase intake of iron, folic acid, and calcium
questions.explanation: Pregnant women need increased iron, folic acid, and calcium for healthy foetal development.

questions.text: Which of these fats is considered the healthiest for cooking?
questions.explanation: Olive oil is rich in monounsaturated fats and is considered one of the healthiest cooking oils.

questions.text: The glycemic index (GI) of a food measures
options: How quickly it raises blood sugar levels
questions.explanation: The glycemic index measures how quickly a carbohydrate-containing food raises blood glucose levels.

questions.text: Which of these is a principle of menu planning for a school canteen?
options: Provide nutritious, affordable, and child-friendly meals
questions.explanation: School canteen menus should be nutritious, affordable, and appealing to children.

questions.text: Which class of food provides the MOST energy per gram?
questions.explanation: Fats provide 9 kcal per gram, more than carbohydrates or proteins which provide 4 kcal each.

questions.text: The process of tempering chocolate involves
options: Melting it completely and letting it set
Carefully heating and cooling to form stable cocoa butter crystals
questions.explanation: Tempering chocolate involves controlled heating and cooling to form stable crystals for a smooth finish.

questions.text: Which of these is a characteristic of vitamin E?
options: Acts as an antioxidant protecting cell membranes
questions.explanation: Vitamin E is a fat-soluble antioxidant that protects cell membranes from oxidative damage.

questions.text: What does the term Mise en place in cooking refer to in animal husbandry?
options: Preparing and organising all ingredients before cooking
questions.explanation: Mise en place means having everything in place - preparing and organising all ingredients before cooking.

questions.text: Which of these is a source of complex carbohydrates?
questions.explanation: Whole wheat is a good source of complex carbohydrates (starch and fibre).

questions.text: Vitamin K is important in the body for
questions.explanation: Vitamin K is essential for proper blood clotting.

questions.text: Which of these is a function of the liver in relation to nutrition?
options: It absorbs vitamins directly from food
It stores vitamins and regulates blood sugar
It grinds food like the teeth
questions.explanation: The liver stores vitamins, detoxifies harmful substances, and helps regulate blood sugar.

questions.text: Which of these is an example of a legume?
questions.explanation: Cowpea is a legume, part of the pulse family which includes beans and lentils.

questions.text: The primary role of carbohydrates in the diet is to
questions.explanation: Carbohydrates are the body's primary and most efficient source of energy.

questions.text: Which of these kitchen tools is used for measuring small amounts of liquid?
questions.explanation: Measuring spoons are used to measure small quantities of liquid or dry ingredients.

questions.text: Which of these is a method of moist heat cooking?
questions.explanation: Stewing is a moist heat cooking method where food is cooked slowly in liquid.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "Scurvy is characterised by" by choosing the correct option.
options: Bleeding gums and poor wound healing
questions.explanation: Scurvy symptoms include bleeding gums, bruising, and poor wound healing.

questions.text: The process of digestion begins in the
questions.explanation: Digestion begins in the mouth where mechanical and chemical digestion starts.

questions.text: Which of these is NOT a food preservation method?
questions.explanation: Emulsification is a mixing technique, not a food preservation method.

questions.text: Which of these is a source of unsaturated fat?
questions.explanation: Avocado is rich in healthy monounsaturated fats, unlike butter and lard which are high in saturated fats.

questions.text: Scurvy was historically common among sailors because they
options: Had no access to fresh fruits and vegetables for long periods
questions.explanation: Sailors on long voyages lacked fresh fruits and vegetables, leading to vitamin C deficiency.

questions.text: Which food group should form the base of a food-based dietary guideline pyramid?
questions.explanation: Carbohydrate-rich staples form the base of dietary guideline pyramids as they should be consumed in the largest amounts.

questions.text: Which of these is an example of a fermented food?
questions.explanation: Ogi is a traditional Nigerian fermented food made from maize.

questions.text: Which of these is a function of water in cooking?
options: It transfers heat to food during boiling and steaming
It acts as a preservative only
questions.explanation: Water transfers heat to food during moist heat cooking methods like boiling and steaming.

questions.text: The main source of energy for the brain is
questions.explanation: The brain primarily uses glucose derived from carbohydrates as its energy source.

questions.text: Which of these is an example of a foodborne pathogen?
questions.explanation: E. coli is a well-known foodborne pathogen that can cause severe illness.

questions.text: Which of these is a function of roughage in the diet?
options: Adds bulk to stool and aids bowel movement
questions.explanation: Roughage adds bulk to stool and helps promote regular bowel movements.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "Toasting is a form of" by choosing the correct option.
questions.explanation: Toasting is a dry heat cooking method that uses direct heat to brown food surfaces.

questions.text: Which of these is a consequence of vitamin D deficiency in children?
questions.explanation: Vitamin D deficiency in children leads to rickets, characterised by soft and weak bones.

questions.text: Which of these is used to make garri, a popular Nigerian food?
questions.explanation: Garri is made from cassava tubers that are peeled, grated, fermented, and fried.

questions.text: The food group that provides the most variety of vitamins is the
questions.explanation: Fruits and vegetables provide the widest variety of vitamins and minerals.

questions.text: Milk is a good source of which mineral?
questions.explanation: Milk is one of the best dietary sources of calcium.

questions.text: Which of these is NOT a kitchen safety practice?
options: Using oven mitts for hot trays
Turning pot handles inward on the stove
questions.explanation: Blunt knives are more dangerous than sharp ones as they require more force and can slip.

questions.text: Which of these is a symptom of food poisoning?
questions.explanation: Food poisoning commonly causes nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, and abdominal pain.

questions.text: Which of these foods is the best source of iron?
questions.explanation: Red meat and liver are excellent sources of heme iron, which is easily absorbed.

questions.text: Starch belongs to which class of carbohydrate?
questions.explanation: Starch is a polysaccharide, a complex carbohydrate made of many glucose units.

questions.text: Which of these is a function of potassium in the body?
options: Maintains fluid balance and nerve function
questions.explanation: Potassium helps maintain fluid balance, nerve function, and muscle contraction.

questions.text: The Maillard reaction requires the presence of
options: Reducing sugars and amino acids under heat
questions.explanation: The Maillard reaction is a chemical reaction between reducing sugars and amino acids at high temperatures.

questions.text: Which of these is a function of the enzyme pepsin in digestion?
options: Breaks down carbohydrates in the mouth
Breaks down proteins in the stomach
questions.explanation: Pepsin is a stomach enzyme that breaks down proteins into peptides.

questions.text: What does Enrichment of food involve in the context of fishing?
options: Adding back nutrients lost during processing
questions.explanation: Enrichment means adding back nutrients that were lost during food processing.

questions.text: Which of these is a reason for food fortification?
options: To improve the nutritional quality of the food supply
To change the taste of food
questions.explanation: Food fortification aims to improve the nutritional quality of the overall food supply.

questions.text: Which of these is an example of emulsification in cooking?
options: Making mayonnaise from oil, egg, and vinegar
questions.explanation: Mayonnaise is an emulsion where oil is dispersed in water (vinegar) using egg yolk as an emulsifier.

questions.text: The term 'al dente' in cooking pasta means
options: Cooked to be firm when bitten
questions.explanation: Al dente means the pasta is cooked to be firm when bitten, not mushy.

questions.text: Which of these is an effect of overcooking vegetables?
options: Loss of heat-sensitive vitamins like vitamin C and B
questions.explanation: Overcooking destroys heat-sensitive vitamins such as vitamin C and B vitamins.

questions.text: What does the term "The term 'sauteing'" mean?
options: Cooking food in a large amount of water
Quickly frying small pieces of food in a small amount of hot fat
Cooking by boiling in salt water
questions.explanation: Sauteing involves quickly frying small pieces of food in a small amount of hot fat while stirring.

questions.text: Which of these is a symptom of vitamin B12 deficiency?
questions.explanation: Vitamin B12 deficiency causes pernicious anaemia, affecting red blood cell formation.

questions.text: Sprouting increases the nutritional value of grains mainly by
options: Increasing vitamin content and improving protein quality
questions.explanation: Sprouting increases vitamin content (especially B vitamins) and improves the digestibility of proteins.

questions.text: Which of these is a principle of food storage?
options: Store raw food above cooked food
Store food in a cool, dry, and clean place
Leave food uncovered at room temperature
questions.explanation: Food should be stored in a cool, dry, and clean place away from contaminants.

questions.text: Which of these is a source of prebiotics in the diet?
questions.explanation: Garlic, onions, and bananas are good sources of prebiotics that feed beneficial gut bacteria.

questions.text: In setting a formal table, the fork is placed
options: To the right of the plate
To the left of the plate
questions.explanation: In formal table setting, the fork is placed to the left of the dinner plate.

questions.text: The number of food groups in a basic food classification system is
questions.explanation: The basic food classification system has 6 food groups.

questions.text: Which of these is a characteristic of a good kitchen layout?
options: Efficient work triangle between stove, sink, and refrigerator
questions.explanation: A good kitchen layout follows the work triangle principle for efficiency between stove, sink, and refrigerator.

questions.text: Which of these is a function of the enzyme amylase?
options: Breaks down fats in the stomach
Breaks down starch into sugar in the mouth
questions.explanation: Amylase, found in saliva, begins the chemical digestion of starch into maltose.

questions.text: Which of these is a health risk of consuming too much saturated fat?
questions.explanation: Excessive saturated fat intake raises LDL cholesterol and increases the risk of heart disease.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "Ceviche is a dish prepared by" by choosing the correct option.
options: Cooking fish in citrus juice (acid denaturation)
questions.explanation: Ceviche involves 'cooking' fish by marinating it in citrus juice, where the acid denatures the proteins.

questions.text: Which of these is a benefit of eating a balanced diet during pregnancy?
options: Supports healthy foetal development and maternal health
Eliminates the need for antenatal care
questions.explanation: A balanced diet during pregnancy supports healthy foetal development and maintains maternal health.

questions.text: Which of these is an example of a disaccharide?
questions.explanation: Lactose is a disaccharide found in milk, composed of glucose and galactose.

questions.text: Which of these is an advantage of using a pressure cooker?
options: Food cooks faster due to increased boiling point of water
It uses less energy but takes longer
It is only used for making soups
questions.explanation: A pressure cooker raises the boiling point of water, cooking food faster than normal boiling.

questions.text: Which of these is a major component of a good feeding programme for an institution?
options: A planned menu that meets the nutritional needs of the target group
questions.explanation: An institutional feeding programme must have a planned menu meeting the nutritional needs of its target group.

questions.text: The process of denaturation of protein involves
options: Unfolding the protein structure due to heat, acid, or alkali
questions.explanation: Denaturation unfolds the protein structure due to heat, acid, or physical action without breaking peptide bonds.

questions.text: Which of these foods would be most suitable for a diabetic patient?
options: Brown rice with vegetables and lean protein
questions.explanation: Brown rice with vegetables and lean protein has a lower glycemic index and better nutritional value.

questions.text: The main difference between baking and roasting is that
options: Baking uses moisture while roasting does not
Baking is mainly for bread and pastries while roasting is for meats and vegetables
Baking uses oil while roasting uses water
questions.explanation: Baking is typically for bread, cakes, and pastries, while roasting is for meats, poultry, and vegetables.

questions.text: Which of these is a source of thiamine (vitamin B1)?
questions.explanation: Whole grains and lean pork are excellent sources of thiamine (vitamin B1).

questions.text: Which of these is a factor that affects the nutrient content of food?
options: The brand of the cooking pot
Method of cooking and duration of cooking
questions.explanation: Cooking method and duration significantly affect the nutrient content of food.

questions.text: An appetiser served before a meal is intended to
questions.explanation: An appetiser is a small dish served before the main meal to stimulate the appetite.

questions.text: Which of these is a characteristic of a healthy eating pattern?
options: Eating a variety of foods from all food groups
Eating only one type of food daily
questions.explanation: Healthy eating involves consuming a variety of foods from all food groups in appropriate amounts.

questions.text: Folate (folic acid) is especially important for
options: Preventing neural tube defects in developing foetuses
questions.explanation: Folic acid is crucial during pregnancy to prevent neural tube defects in the developing foetus.

questions.text: Which of these is a safe food thawing method?
options: Thawing at room temperature on the counter
Leaving frozen food in the sun
questions.explanation: Thawing in the refrigerator is the safest method as it keeps food out of the temperature danger zone.

questions.text: The main reason for adding salt during cooking is to
options: Enhance flavour and taste of food
questions.explanation: Salt is primarily added to enhance the flavour and taste of food during cooking.

questions.text: Which of these is a Nigerian fermented beverage?
questions.explanation: Pito is a traditional Nigerian fermented beverage made from millet or sorghum.

questions.text: Which of these is a function of lymph nodes in relation to nutrition?
options: Filter pathogens from food absorbed through the gut
questions.explanation: Lymph nodes help filter pathogens from substances absorbed through the digestive tract.

questions.text: The best way to preserve the vitamin C content of vegetables is to
options: Boil them for a long time
Cook them quickly with minimal water
Dry them in the sun for days
questions.explanation: Quick cooking with minimal water helps preserve heat-sensitive and water-soluble vitamin C.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "A weaning food should be" by choosing the correct option.
questions.explanation: Weaning foods should be soft, smooth in texture, and rich in nutrients for the transitioning infant.

questions.text: Which of these is a cause of food waste in the kitchen?
options: Over-preparing food and poor storage practices
questions.explanation: Over-preparing food and poor storage are major causes of food waste in the kitchen.

questions.text: Which of these is a characteristic of a good cookbook?
options: Clear ingredients list and step-by-step instructions
Recipes written in a foreign language only
questions.explanation: A good cookbook provides a clear ingredients list and detailed step-by-step instructions.

questions.text: Which of these is a source of selenium in the diet?
questions.explanation: Brazil nuts and seafood are among the richest dietary sources of selenium.

questions.text: Dietary reference intake (DRI) is a set of
options: Reference values for nutrient intake to maintain health
questions.explanation: DRI provides reference values for nutrient intake needed to maintain health in different age groups.

questions.text: Which of these is an example of a monosaccharide?
questions.explanation: Fructose is a monosaccharide (simple sugar) found naturally in fruits.

questions.text: The role of sebum produced by the skin in relation to vitamin D is to
options: Help absorb UV light for vitamin D synthesis
questions.explanation: Sebum on the skin helps facilitate the absorption of UV light needed for vitamin D synthesis.

questions.text: Which of these is a health benefit of dietary fibre?
options: Reduces the risk of colon cancer and heart disease
questions.explanation: Adequate dietary fibre intake reduces the risk of colon cancer, heart disease, and helps manage weight.

questions.text: Which of these is a correct food safety temperature for holding hot food?
questions.explanation: Hot food should be held above 63C to prevent bacterial growth.

questions.text: Which of these is a characteristic of good food presentation?
options: Food piled randomly on the plate
Neat arrangement with attention to colour and garnish
questions.explanation: Good food presentation involves neat arrangement with attention to colour, garnish, and plate cleanliness.

questions.text: Which of these is a property of proteins in cooking?
options: They dissolve completely in cold water
questions.explanation: Proteins coagulate (set and harden) when heated, which is why eggs solidify when cooked.

questions.text: A person who avoids all animal products is following a
questions.explanation: A vegan diet excludes all animal products including meat, dairy, and eggs.

questions.text: Which of these is a source of simple sugars in the diet?
questions.explanation: Honey and table sugar are sources of simple sugars (monosaccharides and disaccharides).

questions.text: Which of these is a disadvantage of deep frying as a cooking method?
options: It uses large amounts of oil which adds excess calories
It cannot be used for any food
questions.explanation: Deep frying uses large amounts of oil, which can significantly increase the calorie content of food.

questions.text: What does The process of making tofu involve in the context of fishing?
options: Coagulating soy milk to form curds
questions.explanation: Tofu is made by coagulating soy milk and pressing the resulting curds into solid blocks.

questions.text: Which of these is a symptom of dehydration?
questions.explanation: Dehydration symptoms include dark-coloured urine, excessive thirst, and dry mouth.

questions.text: Which of these is a recommended practice for knife safety?
options: Cut on a stable, non-slip cutting board
Carry knives with the blade facing outward
questions.explanation: Always cut on a stable, non-slip cutting board to prevent accidents.

questions.text: Which of these is a major nutrient found in eggs?
questions.explanation: Eggs are an excellent source of high-quality protein and contain healthy fats and various vitamins.

questions.text: Which of these is a characteristic of a malnourished child?
options: Stunted growth, weakened immunity, and developmental delays
questions.explanation: Malnutrition causes stunted growth, weakened immunity, and delayed physical and cognitive development.

questions.text: Which of these is a benefit of eating breakfast?
options: It provides energy and improves concentration for the day's activities
It is not necessary for adults
It replaces the need for lunch
questions.explanation: Eating breakfast provides essential energy and improves concentration and productivity.

questions.text: The process of caramelisation involves
options: Boiling sugar in water until it turns brown
Freezing sugar at very low temperatures
questions.explanation: Caramelisation is the browning of sugar when heated, producing a distinctive flavour and colour.

questions.text: Which of these is an important principle of menu pricing?
options: Always set the highest possible price
Consider food cost, labour, overhead, and profit margin
questions.explanation: Menu pricing should consider food cost, labour, overhead costs, and a reasonable profit margin.

questions.text: The role of folate in the body includes
options: Cell division and formation of red blood cells
questions.explanation: Folate plays a crucial role in cell division and the formation of red blood cells.

questions.text: Which of these is an example of a complete meal?
options: Jollof rice with chicken, vegetables, and fruit salad
questions.explanation: Jollof rice with chicken, vegetables, and fruit salad provides carbohydrates, protein, vitamins, and minerals.

questions.text: Which of these is a food preservation method that uses salt?
questions.explanation: Curing uses salt (and sometimes sugar and nitrates) to preserve meats and fish.

questions.text: The food safety management system used in food industries is called
questions.explanation: HACCP is a systematic food safety management system used in food industries to identify and control hazards.

questions.text: Which of these foods is rich in vitamin E?
questions.explanation: Sunflower seeds and wheat germ are excellent sources of vitamin E.

questions.text: The purpose of garnishing food is to
options: Enhance visual appeal and add complementary flavours
questions.explanation: Garnishing enhances the visual appeal of food and can add complementary flavours.

questions.text: Which of these is a risk of consuming excessive vitamin A?
options: Hypervitaminosis A causing liver damage and headaches
questions.explanation: Excessive vitamin A intake can cause hypervitaminosis A, leading to liver damage, nausea, and headaches.

questions.text: Which of these is a role of magnesium in the body?
options: Supports muscle and nerve function and bone health
questions.explanation: Magnesium supports muscle and nerve function, blood sugar regulation, and bone health.

questions.text: Which of these is a characteristic of a food handler's hygiene?
options: Wearing clean uniforms, hairnets, and washing hands regularly
Handling money and food with the same hands
questions.explanation: Food handlers must wear clean uniforms and hairnets, and wash hands regularly to prevent contamination.

questions.text: The importance of reading food labels includes
options: Knowing ingredients, nutritional values, expiry dates, and allergens
questions.explanation: Food labels provide essential information about ingredients, nutrition, expiry dates, and potential allergens.

questions.text: Which of these is the correct order of the digestive system?
options: Mouth, oesophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine
questions.explanation: The correct order is mouth, oesophagus, stomach, small intestine, and large intestine.
